package.title: Tempo.Reporting.Abstractions
package.description: Contracts, JSON definition schema, validation models, data provider interfaces, and server DTOs for Tempo Reporting. No Blazor or ASP.NET dependency.

gettingStarted.title: Getting Started with Tempo.Reporting.Abstractions
gettingStarted.overview: Tempo.Reporting.Abstractions contains the report definition model, validation contracts, tenant-aware data provider interfaces, report definition storage contracts, report server DTOs, and the typed HTTP client used by remote Blazor reporting components.

programCs.description: Register the typed report server client when a host communicates with Tempo.ReportServer.Api.

notes: The package has no Blazor or ASP.NET dependency and is safe to reference from API, worker, shared DTO, and embedded-report projects.
Report server request and response DTOs live here so Blazor clients, external applications, and the server share one contract.

items.description: Payload of the Blazor host's same-origin GET /auth/token hand-out endpoint: a short-lived access token plus its absolute expiry. The WebAssembly leg caches this in memory only and re-fetches when it nears expiry. The refresh token is never part of this payload — it stays in the server-side token store.

Base class for typed HTTP clients that call the Tempo Report Server API from either Blazor runtime. It attaches the bearer token per request, read from the consuming scope's IAccessTokenProvider, and performs the standard 401 → force-refresh → retry once step.

Supplies the current user's API access token in whichever runtime the calling component happens to execute (InteractiveServer circuit or InteractiveWebAssembly). Implemented once per host — ServerAccessTokenProvider on the Blazor host and WasmAccessTokenProvider in the WebAssembly leg — and consumed behind this single abstraction so typed API clients never know which runtime produced the token. This is the IdP-agnostic seam: how the token is obtained at login is app-specific; everything downstream only depends on this contract.

The importer is namespace-agnostic: RDL elements are matched by their local name, so the SSRS 2008 / 2010 / 2016 schema namespaces (which differ only by year) and Telerik-namespaced RDL all parse where their element vocabulary overlaps.

items.description: Validates AddReportFavoriteRequestDto for the favorites endpoint. Messages are TmResources KEYS (resolved by the caller/UI localizer) so the validator is reusable by the Blazor front end without depending on a server-side string localizer.

Validates CreateReportRequestDto for the report-create endpoint and the portal's new-report form. Like the favorites validator, messages are TmResources KEYS (resolved by the caller/UI localizer, e.g. the localized report-server portal), so the validator is reusable by the Blazor front end without depending on a server-side string localizer. The API host reuses the same validator for a 400 response, so that body carries the resource key rather than English prose.
